rows.selection_reason: With zero completed experiments, there is no evidence to exploit, so the priority is establishing a clean performance floor. config_001 (RNA-only, single-profile, PCA-2000) is the simplest configuration in the design space: no image branch, no aggregation, no fusion, and a standard linear encoder. It isolates the RNA modality under the least confounded settings, giving a well-defined baseline against which every other design axis (image modality, multiprofile aggregation, learned encoders like scVI/scGPT, and fusion strategy) can later be evaluated as a controlled increment. Choosing this first experiment maximizes the interpretability of all subsequent comparisons and avoids committing to any complex design choice before we know the unimodal, single-profile reference performance.

We have only one completed experiment (config_001: RNA-only, single profile, PCA → ~48.5% accuracy), so uncertainty is high across all design axes. The most fundamental open question is whether the image modality carries useful signal for this task at all. Config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) directly tests this while keeping the profile setting identical to config_001 (singleprofile), making the comparison as clean as possible across modalities. Knowing the image-only ceiling is essential before investing budget in multimodal fusion experiments: if image alone performs poorly, multimodal gains are unlikely and we should instead focus on improving the RNA encoder (scvi, scgpt) or multiprofile aggregation. Conversely, if image alone is competitive or strong, it justifies prioritizing multimodal configurations. This single experiment reduces the largest source of uncertainty in the search space and is the highest-information-per-experiment choice under a tight budget.

Evidence: RNA (pca_n2000, singleprofile) achieves 48.5% accuracy while image (resnet50, singleprofile) is weak at 20.8%, making RNA the dominant modality and the primary target for improvement. Uncertainty: We do not yet know whether the multiprofile structure (multiple profiles per cell) plus aggregation carries meaningful signal beyond a single profile. This experiment (config_002) isolates that question by changing only the profile setting from singleprofile to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, keeping the same pca_n2000 encoder as config_001. If accuracy improves, it confirms that profile structure matters and motivates testing transformer aggregation (config_003) and multiprofile with better encoders. If it does not improve, we learn that the bottleneck is encoder quality rather than profile structure, redirecting effort toward scvi/scgpt encoders. This is the most informative single-variable extension of our best result under a tight budget.

Evidence: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) achieved 0.591 acc, a large +10.6 pt gain over the singleprofile baseline (config_001, 0.485 acc), confirming that multiprofile structure carries substantial signal. However, we have only tested one aggregation method (avgpool). Uncertainty: it is unknown whether a transformer-based aggregation, which can model cell-to-cell relationships within a profile, can further exploit the multiprofile structure beyond simple averaging. This experiment (config_003) isolates exactly one variable—aggregation (transformer vs avgpool)—while holding model setting, profile setting, and RNA encoder (pca_n2000) constant, making it a clean comparison. It is the best use of the next budget slot because it directly extends our strongest result with a single, well-motivated change; if transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool, it identifies a high-value design axis to build on, and if it does not, we confirm avgpool sufficiency and can redirect effort toward encoder choice or multimodal fusion without having wasted an experiment on a confounded comparison.

Evidence: config_002 (RNA, multi-profile, PCA, avgpool) is the current best at 0.591 acc, and we've established that multi-profile + avgpool is the strongest RNA-only setting. However, we have only tested one RNA encoder (PCA n2000), leaving uncertainty about whether a learned representation could further improve performance. Question: config_005 (RNA, multi-profile, scvi_n200, avgpool) changes only the RNA encoder relative to config_002, cleanly isolating the encoder effect while holding profile setting and aggregation constant. Why this is the best next experiment: It directly tests whether the linear PCA representation is a bottleneck or whether a non-linear learned embedding (scVI) captures additional biological signal. If scvi outperforms PCA, it justifies investing further in learned encoders (including scgpt) and multimodal fusion with richer RNA features. If it underperforms, it confirms PCA is sufficient and redirects budget toward fusion strategy or image modality questions. This single-variable comparison maximizes information gain per experiment under the limited budget.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 acc. We have strong evidence that multiprofile+avgpool is the best profile/aggregation combination (avgpool beats transformer by 0.072 for PCA; multiprofile beats singleprofile by 0.106). However, the RNA encoder dimension is only partially explored: PCA (0.591) and scvi_n200 (0.650) are tested, but scgpt is completely untested. Question: Does scgpt, with its pretrained single-cell generative architecture, produce a better or worse representation than scvi_n200 under the same multiprofile+avgpool setting? This is a clean single-variable comparison against config_005. Why this is the best next experiment: The aggregation question (avgpool vs transformer) is relatively well-answered with a large margin, while the encoder choice is a high-impact, under-explored dimension. Testing scgpt at the best-known profile/aggregation settings isolates the encoder effect and could reveal whether a third encoder option outperforms scvi_n200, which would significantly change the search direction for subsequent multimodal experiments.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_005 (RNA-only, scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) at 0.650 acc / 0.628 F1. Image-only with resnet50 was very weak (0.208), but we have not yet tested whether adding image features to the strong RNA signal via fusion can provide complementary information. The key uncertainty is whether multimodal fusion improves over the best unimodal model, which is the central question of this study. Config_030 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, concat) is the minimal, logical extension of config_005: it keeps every RNA-side setting at its best-known value and adds only the image modality with the simplest fusion (concat). This isolates the effect of adding image information to the strongest RNA pipeline. If it improves, we have a new best and a clear direction for exploring fusion type and image encoder. If it does not, we learn that resnet50 image features do not complement scvi RNA representations, redirecting effort toward either a stronger image encoder (ViT-L) or RNA-only refinements. Under the limited budget, this single experiment directly answers the highest-value question—does multimodal fusion help?—using the most validated component settings available.

Evidence: config_005 (RNA-only, scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) achieved 0.650 acc, while config_030 (multimodal, scvi_n200, resnet50, multiprofile, avgpool, concat) dropped to 0.632 acc—adding the image modality with simple concatenation actually hurt performance. This is the most surprising and consequential finding so far. Question: config_031 changes only the fusion strategy from concat to weighted, keeping all other settings identical to config_030. This isolates whether the performance drop is due to the fusion mechanism (concat forcing equal-weight combination of a strong RNA signal with a weak ResNet50 signal) or due to the image features themselves being uninformative/noisy. Why best next experiment: It is a clean single-variable A/B comparison against config_030, directly addressing the key open question of whether the image modality can contribute value under proper integration. If weighted fusion recovers to ≥0.650, it reveals the image carries signal that needs gating; if it stays near 0.632, it strongly indicates ResNet50 features are not useful for this task, redirecting effort toward RNA-only optimization or a stronger image encoder (ViT-L). No other available configuration answers this question with fewer confounds.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_031 (multimodal, scvi_n200, ResNet50, avgpool, weighted) at 0.678 acc, only modestly above RNA-only scvi_n200 (config_005, 0.650). ResNet50 alone is very weak (0.208), raising the question of whether the image modality has meaningful additional signal that ResNet50 simply cannot extract. Question: config_037 swaps the image encoder from ResNet50 to ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L while holding all other settings (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion) identical to config_031. This isolates the image-encoder effect. Why this is the best next experiment: (1) It is a clean single-variable extension of the current best configuration, directly testing whether the modest +0.028 gain from adding ResNet50 reflects a ceiling in the image encoder or a true ceiling in the image modality's complementary signal. (2) If ViT-L substantially improves over ResNet50, it identifies a promising direction for further multimodal optimization; if it does not, it tells us the image modality contributes little beyond RNA and we should focus remaining budget on RNA-side improvements. (3) Under a limited budget, resolving whether the image channel is worth further investment is more consequential than confirming the already-suggested avgpool>transformer aggregation preference.

The best configuration so far is config_037 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) at 0.7062 acc. The only untested dimension in this top-performing setup is aggregation: we have strong evidence that avgpool > transformer for pca_n2000 RNA (config_002: 0.5907 vs config_003: 0.5191), but scvi_n200 produces a fundamentally different (lower-dimensional, learned) representation where transformer aggregation might interact differently. Config_039 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding all other factors at their best-known values (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, weighted fusion, multiprofile). This is a clean single-variable comparison against config_037 that will clarify whether aggregation is a meaningful design axis in the best multimodal regime. If it improves, we identify a new best; if it does not, we confirm avgpool is optimal and can redirect budget to other unexplored dimensions (e.g., scgpt encoders or image-only multiprofile baselines) with confidence that aggregation is settled.
